alex: quick heads-up — ran nsys on staging (batch=32, seq=512). seeing a surprising time concentration in fused_attn_forward_v2 and an unusual kv_index_lookup kernel. output snippet:
```
nsys profile -o run1 --trace=cuda,cublas python perf/serve_bench.py --batch 32
# summary (GPU time %):
  fused_attn_forward_v2    62.4%
  kv_index_lookup          18.7%
  gemm_small               10.1%
  other                    8.8%
```
Anyone seen this kv_index_lookup climb after the recent batching tweaks?

mira: Seen something similar on the quantized path. Could be our new batching heuristics that group by seq len causing more random KV lookups — increased L2 thrash. Can you attach the perfetto timeline? :mag_right: 

alex: uploaded trace to gs://redwood-traces/1932109876-perfetto.zip and started perf-bot analysis. perf-bot: please post flamegraph when ready.

perf-bot: Perfetto analysis complete. Top timeline spans: fused_attn_forward_v2 (dominant, long-running kernels with high SM idle between launches), kv_index_lookup (many small launches, high launch overhead). flame graph saved -> gs://redwood-traces/flame_1932109876.svg

li: Short thought — fused_attn has high theoretical occupancy but low SM util due to warp divergence at mid-range seqs. kv_index is launch-heavy — tiny kernels causing notable launch overhead and CPU scheduling pressure. Two levers: (1) fuse small KV lookups into a batched kernel, (2) increase batching window or group requests more aggressively to amortize launch cost. Also consider coalesced KV layout to reduce random loads.

sam: Agreed. Also check kernel selector fallback: it sometimes picks small_gemm for shapes that would benefit from batched_gemm when seq distribution is skewed. I have a prototype patch that biases the selector by batch-time ratio (trade latency vs throughput). I'll open a PR.

mira: Would like a microbenchmark matrix: seq=64/128/512 distributions, measure per-token p50/p95 and kernel launch counts. I can spin that up and run perfetto + nvprof variants. :white_check_mark: 

alex: Quick nvprof capture for a single request (seq 512) shows:
```
GPU activities:
  fused_attn_forward_v2  45.2ms  68%
  kv_index_lookup        12.3ms  18%
  launch_overhead         5.8ms   9%
```
so launch overhead isn't negligible even for single-request profiles.

li: :point_up: launch overhead likely from many tiny kernels in kv path. Suggest combining lookup + gather + scatter into one kernel that operates over batch*head dims to reduce launches and improve memory coalescing.

sam: Also seeing a perf regression on nightly after commit c3f5a — attaching bisect notes to the PR. If it's that commit we can revert the selector tweak quickly and revert to previous heuristics.

mira: I'll run the microbenchmarks and post numbers & trace ids by EOD. If confirmed, revert selector and land a more conservative heuristic that avoids small_gemm for batched shapes.

alex: Thanks. Action items: @sam open PR for selector change, @li prototype fused KV kernel, @mira run microbench and post trace ids. :thumbsup: 

dave: small note — let's add an alert to detect the "many small kernels" pattern in the tracing pipeline so we catch regressions earlier. I can add a perf-lint check that flags high kernel-count + small average durations.

alex: perfect, thanks all. will follow up after microbench results.
